changelog: Delete C2: remove a redundant principle that restates predicate-argument and attachment concerns already covered by C3, to prune attention and satisfy the 'prune' constraint.
findings: The prompt routinely ranks cuts too high when they separate a finite verb/coproduct/auxiliary from the words that complete its core argument, producing orphaned predicates or scope flips.

edits.was: - If the pieces are translated independently and concatenated, will the joined t

diagnosis.why: Deleting C2 removed a constraint that discouraged cuts which would split concatenation-sensitive or predicate/argument chunks; as a result the model more often moves cuts earlier or into noun/verb phrases (e.g. splitting 'you are using a satellite' into 'a ‖ satellite' or breaking 'We will' into 'We ‖ will'), which slightly helped the very-short bin (≤3) but produced net harm in medium-length pieces (≤10 and up) and only a marginal overall gain with CI crossing zero. The small drop in rank-1 frequency and increases at deeper ranks show the revision dispersed top cut mass, producing more internal splits.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should respect that the deleted C2 constraint matters — do not remove the guidance that prevents cutting inside concatenation-sensitive or predicate/argument units, because its removal increases harmful internal splits in medium-length pieces.
